stories.summary: The Buffalo Bills host the Detroit Lions in their first game at their new home, Highmark Stadium. Here are all the highlights from Bills vs. Lions in Buffalo.
stories.body:
NFL Week 2 action begins with the Buffalo Bills breaking in their brand-new home, Highmark Stadium, against the visiting Detroit Lions on Thursday night.

Both teams enter the contest following nail-biting victories. Buffalo pulled off a last-second win over the Houston Texans in Week 1, forcing a C.J. Stroud fumble on the Texans' last drive of the game to secure a 36-31 win. Meanwhile, the Lions needed to go to overtime to get past the New Orleans Saints. After being held scoreless in the first half, the Saints stormed back to tie the game at 24-24 at the end of regulation before losing 31-30 on a failed 2-point conversion.

Follow along for all the updates and highlights from the Bills' home debut in Highmark Stadium.

stories.headline: Austin scores 20, Iraifen has 18 points and 11 rebounds, Mystics beat Sky 110-80
stories.summary: — Shakira Austin scored 20 points, Kiki Iriafen finished with 18 points and 11 rebounds, and the Washington Mystics beat the Chicago Sky 110-80 on Thursday night in their first game since the FIBA World Cup break.
stories.body:
CHICAGO -- — Shakira Austin scored 20 points, Kiki Iriafen finished with 18 points and 11 rebounds, and the Washington Mystics beat the Chicago Sky 110-80 on Thursday night in their first game since the FIBA World Cup break.


The Mystics (25-16), tied with Dallas for sixth in the WNBA standings, moved a half-game ahead of New York. The top four have home court advantage in the best-of-three first round of the playoffs, which begin Sept. 27.


Courtney Vandersloot led Chicago with 14 points and Sydney Taylor scored 12. Kamilla Cardoso and Gabriela Jaquez each added 10 points.


Iriafen, who had her 21st double-double this season, grabbed four offensive rebounds to set a franchise single-season record with 115.


Austin made a layup in the opening minute to break Washington’s single-season scoring record. The 6-foot-5 center went into the game with 657 points this season, which tied the previous mark set by Sonia Citron in 2025.


Georgia Amoore and Michaela Onyenwere added 12 points apiece and Cotie McMahon scored 11 for the Mystics. Citron (personal reasons) did not play.


The Sky (15-26) have lost four in a row following a season-high three consecutive wins.


DiJonai Carrington (foot) did not play for Chicago.


Up next 
Mystics: Play Sunday at Indiana.


Sky: Visit Atlanta on Saturday.

stories.headline: Jalen Brunson to guest star on 'Law & Order: SVU' episode in November
stories.summary: NBC announced Thursday that Jalen Brunson will appear in the season's fifth episode, which is scheduled to air Nov. 5.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- Knicks star Jalen Brunson will make a guest-starring appearance on "Law & Order: SVU" this fall.

NBC announced Thursday that Brunson will appear in the season's fifth episode, which is scheduled to air Nov. 5. Details on Brunson's role weren't revealed. Cameras caught Brunson on the show's set in Brooklyn on Wednesday.

Brunson is already set to host the season premiere of "Saturday Night Live" on Sept. 26. He made an appearance Monday in the opening of the Emmy Awards telecast that was hosted by "Law & Order: SVU" star Mariska Hargitay.

Hargitay is a Knicks fan who attended Game 4 of the NBA Finals as New York rallied from a 29-point deficit to beat the San Antonio Spurs 107-106 at Madison Square Garden, a victory that sparked the Knicks to their first title since 1973. Hargitay and Brunson hugged on the court after the game.

The two stars share a mutual friendship, posing at the 2025 Tribeca Film Festival together. Brunson supported Hargitay during her Broadway performance in "Every Brilliant Thing" in June. Hargitay also appeared on Brunson's bus, alongside his father and wife, during the Knicks' championship parade.

stories.headline: Maresca has been pushing all the right buttons in perfect Man City start
stories.summary: Despite using an alternative team, Manchester City made it six wins from six under Enzo Maresca, highlighting just how smoothly the post-Pep Guardiola era has begun.
stories.body:
MANCHESTER, England -- Enzo Maresca could not have drawn up a more perfect start at Manchester City.

There's still a long way to go before the Italian proves he's up to the task of succeeding Pep Guardiola. But after six games and six wins, it's so far, so good.

On Thursday night, Norwich City were dispatched 5-0 in the Carabao Cup. Maresca rested key players, gave valuable minutes to others and booked a place in the next round. It could not have gone any better -- much like Maresca's first few weeks in the job.

He admitted in his pre-match news conference on Wednesday that it was "normal that fans have doubts" when a new man comes in to replace a legendary head coach.

Still only September, the uncertainty is likely to persist a little longer. But with each positive result, it dissipates a little more. Supporters won't have learned much from a comprehensive victory over a much-changed English League Championship team.

But it all adds to the feeling that things are going well. If nothing else, Maresca looks like a man who knows exactly what he's doing.

"I'm very happy with these six games in a row, but now the main focus is just on the next one and I'm not thinking that we won six in a row because they're finished," he said.

"The focus is on the next one and then we have the international break.

"I'm not thinking more than one week ahead because I know that in our job many things can change in one week.

"When we started the season, I was not thinking where we could be in six or seven games. Game after game. Tonight we are happy, many reasons and we can start to think about Sunday."

A Norwich team with one eye on Bolton Wanderers at the weekend was never going to cause City too many problems. Still, Maresca got his team selection right, mixing fringe players in need of a game with exciting academy prospects.

With Erling Haaland rested, Floyd Samba started up front. It took the 17-year-old just 29 minutes to score on his debut. With less than an hour on the clock, he had two.

"To get a debut like that is mind-blowing," said Samba, son of former Blackburn Rovers defender Chris Samba.

"I couldn't be happier right now, being my first senior debut, you have to expect everything to go well, the intensity, the level of players, everything goes up and you have to be able to match it and cope with it, and I think I did well with that."

Behind him, Rayan Cherki started, but he was only needed for 45 minutes. It was still enough time for the Frenchman to score his third goal of the season.

Ayyoub Bouaddi got another taste of England with the security of 32-year-old Mateo Kovacic next to him. Nico O'Reilly was eased back in after injury.

Brazilian winger Allan made his first appearance after arriving from Palmeiras in the summer and got a goal and an assist. Gerónimo Rulli, another recruit, stood in for Gianluigi Donnarumma. Ryan McAidoo, 18, came off the bench to score the fifth.

It was a night for the squad players. And as Maresca pointed out this week, they could all be important when injuries and suspensions begin to pile up in January, February and March.

Where City will be at that point in the season is anyone's guess. It's still a new manager trying to build a team with a lot of new players. But the early signs are good.

There have been statement wins over FC Porto and Manchester United. The performance at Old Trafford with 10 men, in particular, showed exactly what Maresca can do as a tactician even in the most difficult of circumstances.

Elliot Anderson has settled in quickly. Haaland is scoring. There have been questions about the defense, but it's now four clean sheets in a row with a mixture of players and combinations. Abdukodir Khusanov and Vitor Reis -- 22 and 20, respectively -- started at center back against Norwich. Marc Guéhi and Rúben Dias are likely to return against Sunderland on Sunday.

"We have different competitions," said Maresca.

"We have many games and we are just at the beginning of the season. The ones that play tonight are going to play Premier League or UEFA Champions League games because the season is long."

There are tougher tests to come. After the extended international break -- itself difficult to manage -- City play Liverpool away and Paris Saint-Germain at home in the space of four days.

Those games, especially coming back-to-back, will be a true measure of City's credentials in the Premier League and Champions League this season. But after six wins in a row to start his reign, Maresca is well set to meet the challenge.

stories.headline: Red Bulls teen Hall undecided on USMNT future despite 1st call-up
stories.summary: New York Red Bulls teenage forward Julian Hall said the decision on his international allegiance was still "not solidified," despite earning a first call-up to the U.S. men's national team on Thursday.
stories.body:
The New York Red Bulls' teenage forward Julian Hall said the decision on his international allegiance was still "not solidified," despite earning a first call-up to the U.S. men's national team on Thursday.

The 18-year-old was one of 13 newcomers named in coach Mauricio Pochettino's first roster since the United States' World Cup exit at the hands of Belgium this summer.

- The USMNT's first post-World Cup squad is missing its biggest summer stars

- Bundesliga breakout star Campbell committed to U.S.

- Sources: USMNT's Luna (knee) set to be sidelined for months

Hall was born in New York City but holds dual U.S. and Polish citizenship, and has been seen wearing the name "Zakrzewski" on the back of his jersey in a nod to his Polish mother.

"I think it's definitely not solidified for me," Hall told The New York Post on Thursday following his first call-up to the USMNT.

"I appreciate the opportunity and I'm going to do as much as I can to make an impact, but I'm definitely still open to my Polish side. That's a side that I cherish a lot, especially because my mom is from there. I wouldn't say it's solidified."

Hall has represented the U.S. at U15 and U17 level but has also been called up to Poland youth national team camps.

He could make his senior debut for the U.S. in the coming weeks. The USMNT will play a series of friendlies against Peru, Chile, Canada and Mexico from Sept. 26 through Oct. 6.

Even if Hall appears in those games, he could still opt to represent Poland. FIFA rules state that a player is only committed to a nation once they have appeared in a competitive game, defined as "a competition for representative teams organized by FIFA or any confederation," for which friendlies do not count.

Speaking to ESPN last month, Hall gave no indication as to which direction he was leaning.

"I have two great nationalities that have been interested," Hall said.

"I grew up with my mom who is Polish and my father's side is American and I respect both nationalities. But right now I've been pretty neutral with my approach to that."

After making his professional debut in 2023, Hall is enjoying a breakout season with the Red Bulls and has nine goals and five assists in 25 MLS appearances.

He will have familiar company when he joins up with the USMNT later this month, with Red Bulls teammate Adri Mehmeti another of those to earn their first call-up on Thursday.

stories.headline: UFC 331 preview and picks: Pantoja sees opportunity in disaster
stories.summary: Top storylines and coaches' analysis for UFC 331 in Los Angeles.
stories.body:
For two and a half years, Alexandre Pantoja ruled the UFC's flyweight division at a level unseen since the historic era of Demetrious Johnson nearly 10 years ago. And yet, the past nine months since his last fight could prove to be the most compelling of Pantoja's career.
The 36-year-old Pantoja (30-6) will challenge Joshua Van (17-2) for the 125-pound championship at UFC 331 inside Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on Saturday. It will be his first appearance since UFC 323 in December, when he lost the belt to Van via TKO after Pantoja suffered a dislocated elbow 26 seconds into the fight. The nature of the loss has led to a feeling of unfinished business between the two fighters going into Saturday's main event.

"As an athlete, yes, I have a TKO loss on my record," Pantoja told ESPN. "I've never lost by TKO or submission before. Nobody had ever finished me. Now, I have that. But personally, as a man? No. I don't believe I have a loss to him."

Pantoja won the title against Brandon Moreno in 2023 and defended the belt four times before meeting Van. He was among the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world at the time. But with a comeback narrative attached to him for this fight, he said there is an added level of excitement.

"For sure, this is an opportunity," Pantoja said. "In my soul, that's the opportunity. Now, I get to fight the champion. He's the champion of the world and I love that. It makes the fight more spicy for me."

Van, 24, has embraced the narrative -- even while cementing himself as the undisputed champion. There are those who say Van needs to defeat Pantoja again to legitimize his championship, but Van's first title defense against Tatsuro Taira in May made discrediting him harder. Taira's ground game posed a real threat to Van, but he ultimately knocked out the Japanese challenger in the fifth round of a matchup that earned fight of the night honors at UFC 328.

The unfinished business, Pantoja's return and Van's undeniable star power mean Saturday's flyweight title fight is shaping up to be the most anticipated 125-pound title fight since Henry Cejudo ended Johnson's nearly five-year title reign in 2018 then defended the flyweight belt against then-bantamweight champion TJ Dillashaw in 2019.

For Pantoja specifically, his worst stroke of bad luck could turn into the greatest night of his career.

"Saturday night is going to be my best night, man," Pantoja said. "I haven't been to work in 10 months. That's why all of these fights, and this one especially, is worth so much. We work for months to just get one night of work. I've recovered my arm. Now I have an opportunity to show everyone what I did in the last 10 months."

More storylines to watch
History isn't in Pantoja's favor
If Alexandre Pantoja is searching for role models to inspire this weekend's quest to reclaim the championship he lost suddenly and painfully last December, he would be wise to look beyond recent history.

Within the past two weeks, two of the UFC's 11 champs -- women's flyweight Valentina Shevchenko and heavyweight Tom Aspinall -- vacated their titles because of health issues. Their paths back to the top of the mountain are as yet uncharted.

Before them, the most recent champions to lose their titles to injuries did not fare well upon their returns. In November 2022, Jiří Procházka vacated the UFC light heavyweight title after hurting his shoulder in training. His successor was Jamahal Hill, who just months after winning the vacant title had to vacate it himself after rupturing an Achilles. As soon as he was healed, Hill was granted an opportunity to reclaim his title and lost. Procházka was given three shots at the 205-pound belt and fell short in all of them.

For a success story, Pantoja must look deeper into UFC championship history to the brutal health issues overcome by Dominick Cruz. While preparing for a bantamweight title defense in May 2012, Cruz tore the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee. He underwent surgery, then had a setback requiring a second ACL surgery six months later. He was scheduled to return in February 2014 but suffered a groin tear in training. Facing another extended recovery, he vacated his title.

Cruz returned that September and won a fight that put him in position for a shot at his old belt. Three months later, he tore his other ACL.

Finally, in February 2016 -- more than four years after his last title fight -- Cruz challenged TJ Dillashaw for the belt and won a split decision. "I had to show something to myself," Cruz said afterward. "That's what this was."

Tsarukyan's chance to set things right again
Arman Tsarukyan was labeled a snubbed man after it was announced that Justin Gaethje and Paddy Pimblett would headline the first UFC card of 2026 with the No. 1 lightweight contender status at stake. It's hard to remember that sentiment now, considering the year Tsarukyan has had.

In the absence of an obvious UFC fight to take, Tsarukyan has wrestled competitively -- mostly in RAF -- 10 times in 2026. He raised his social media presence exponentially behind videos of lavish cars, extraordinary meals and collaborations with content creator Nina Drama. This is the longest layoff of his UFC career, but his brand has grown more during that time off than from any single fight.

He appears in a good position to get back to work and finally earn the title shot many have said he should have already had. But it won't be an easy fight. Tsarukyan's opponent, Mauricio Ruffy, is a dangerous underdog (+270, according to DraftKings). This fight will restore the order the top of the 155-pound division has lacked in Tsarukyan's absence, regardless of who wins.

Another step for Steveson?

Any MMA prospect would almost certainly switch places with 26-year-old UFC newcomer Gable Steveson. When you're an Olympic gold medal wrestler, and one of the most touted heavyweight prospects in MMA history, certain opportunities are going to come to you that others aren't afforded. It also means Steveson's window for error is small, as he's asked to learn and develop under the sport's brightest lights.

The UFC is managing his opposition. For his second UFC appearance (and fifth pro fight overall), he'll take on Sean Sharaf, a 33-year-old with two knockout losses in his first two UFC fights. Steveson will once again be a heavy, heavy favorite (-2100 by DraftKings), as he was for his promotional debut in July. The heavyweight division is wide open now that Tom Aspinall has vacated his title and the list of top contenders is thin, so Steveson's performance probably means more than the result. If he continues to look the part, his career trajectory could be accelerated at a rate few see.

Coaches' questions and predictions
"Can Pantoja bank enough rounds on the ground, while staying responsible on the feet?"

What a fight this will be. Van shows up in big moments; he's just a proven gamer. If Pantoja stands with Van, he's going to get hurt. Pantoja is good at applying pressure and landing the 1-2 punch (lead left jab, right cross), but he cannot play that game with Van, because of Van's counterboxing. Van's hands are too fast. Van can land four-to-six shots at a time in close distance, and that's something Pantoja really has to watch for. Van is going to have confidence in his ability to get off the ground from his last fight against Taira. I'm going to stay on the fence and say it's a pick 'em. After watching Van's fight with Taira, though, knowing how good Taira is on the ground, it's a little unfair to say Van can't weather the storm on the ground with Pantoja. -- Sayif Saud, Fortis MMA

Prediction: Too close to call

"How big of a setback is Pantoja's injury at age 36?"
Van is young, fired up and he's got bricks in his hands. We've seen some small weaknesses in his game, which are obviously due to lack of experience. He's getting better all the time. If Pantoja comes back and is anywhere close to where he was when he was holding the belt, I think he gets it back. There are just too many variables on the ground. We saw Van get mounted by Taira. Van is going to go to work on fixing that hole in his game, but Pantoja is so good. The biggest question is how bad of a setback is Pantoja's injury, at this stage of his career? He's not a spring chicken. But if he's the same Pantoja, he gets the win, potentially by submission. -- John Wood, Syndicate MMA

Prediction: Pantoja by decision or submission

"Can Ruffy stop takedowns and keep space?"

Arman has been on such a tear with the wrestling in RAF, showing his ability to wrestle bigger guys and show his power and skill in grappling. When it comes to that, he is very dangerous. Ruffy is finding his groove, and he's very sharp on the feet, but former opponents King Green and Michael Chandler don't pose the same grappling threat that Arman poses. I think Benoît Saint Denis kind of exposed that hole in Ruffy's game. It's not to say Ruffy doesn't have a chance. In space, he is a problem. He can absolutely starch Arman in space. But how does he keep a powerhouse like Arman at distance? -- Saud

Prediction: Tsarukyan by decision

"Has Ruffy improved his ground defense enough?"
This is a really interesting fight. Arman is going to want to grind out Ruffy. Arman is easily a top-five wrestler/grappler in the UFC. The one thing about Arman -- even though he's stayed busy with the wrestling appearances, he's been out of the UFC for a while, so it'll be interesting to see how he looks. But unless Ruffy catches him and knocks him out, Arman is a good striker, too. Arman can go the distance in a hard fight. My gut leans to Arman. I'm a big fan of Ruffy, but it's just that grappling prowess of Arman. -- Wood

Prediction: Tsarukyan by decision

ESPN's Jeff Wagenheim contributed to this story.

stories.headline: Lewis Hamilton shuts down asking Ferrari to make changes: 'Never asked for anyone to be replaced'
stories.summary: Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eight world championship is over.
stories.body:
Lewis Hamilton denied he has called for replacements at Ferrari after he admitted his bid for a record eighth world championship is over.

Hamilton threw in the title towel at last weekend's Spanish Grand Prix after he retired from the race in Madrid with a brake problem.

His failure to finish leaves him 101 points behind Kimi Antonelli in the championship standings -- the equivalent of more than four victories -- with just nine scheduled rounds left.

A report in Italy claimed Hamilton has challenged Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur to make changes to the team's trackside staff.

But in a story posted to his Instagram account on Thursday, the 41-year-old wrote: "I've seen some of the stories that have gone out and I want to clear it up on here.

"I've never asked for anyone on my team to be replaced. Everyone I work with works hard every day, and their dedication is what moves us forward.

"I always try to empower and lift people to be the best versions of themselves or at least see the best in themselves.

"I may not always achieve that but it's my intention and what I'm here to do. We all work together and that will continue."

- Lando Norris backs 'exciting' 2027 Monaco GP sprint weekend but 'tougher for us drivers'

- Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time after winning crazy challenge

- F1 2027 calendar: Monaco GP gets sprint race, Türkiye and Portugal return to schedule

Hamilton sparked hope of challenging Antonelli -- the driver who replaced him at Mercedes -- when he won in Barcelona in June.

However, the British driver has not finished on the podium at the past five rounds and has been openly critical of his team's race tactics.

He also took aim at teammate Charles Leclerc's driving after an opening-lap clash in Monza earlier this month. Hamilton said he led face-to-face talks with the Monegasque to clear the air.

His retirement in Madrid marked his first of the campaign, and when asked to assess his title chances, Hamilton replied: "There's no stopping him [Antonelli] and Mercedes this year. They've done a phenomenal job, and they deserve it [the championship]."

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: NRL Midweek Mail semifinals: Bulldogs move to lock away rising rookie
stories.summary: Ronaldo Mulitalo is determined to honour his departing Sharks teammates, Sione Katoa has opened up about his future at the Cowboys and his finals days at the Sharks, while Nathan Cleary is fighting the clock to be fit for Penrith's prelim.
stories.body:
The NRL rarely stands still.

Between training sessions, media appearances, and behind-the-scenes conversations, new storylines often begin to emerge before the weekend arrives.

Throughout the week, ESPN will be gathering notes, insights, and updates from around the competition heading into the NRL's semifinal week.

Bulldogs move early to lock down rising forward

The Bulldogs have moved early to lock down rising forward Alekolasimi 'AJ' Jones, with the club's Rookie of the Year agreeing to a two-year contract extension.

ESPN understands Jones, who was already contracted through the 2027 season, has agreed to a new deal that will keep him at Belmore beyond his existing contract.

The move ensures Jones' future is secured before he would have been free to negotiate with rival clubs for 2028 from November 1.

Kennedy backs Hynes amid criticism

Will Kennedy believes Nicho Hynes has grown from the criticism that has followed him throughout his career, praising the Sharks star ahead of their semi-final against the Roosters.

"He's learned a lot from all the criticism he gets and he's taken a step forward," Kennedy said. "For me, I just want to get around him because he's my brother and I want to play next to him."

Trindall 'really good' after shoulder scare

Will Kennedy says Braydon Trindall has pulled up well after battling through a shoulder issue in Cronulla's finals win over North Queensland.

Kennedy said Trindall had been "really dialled in on the mental side" of his game and indicated the halfback had told him he was feeling "really good" ahead of the Roosters clash.

Mulitalo relishing 'Marky Mark' rematch

Ronaldo Mulitalo is embracing another blockbuster battle with Roosters star Mark Nawaqanitawase, describing the departing winger as a "generational talent".

Mulitalo said Nawaqanitawase "brings the best out of me" and revealed their on-field rivalry is largely one-sided when it comes to the verbal exchanges.

"He's a gentleman out there... he doesn't really say anything. I think it's more myself," Mulitalo joked. "He knows I'm just going to keep talking, so he just ignores me anyway."

Mulitalo determined to honour departing Sharks

Ronaldo Mulitalo says Cronulla's finals run carries added significance with several longtime teammates set to leave the club at season's end.

Mulitalo said he has played alongside some of the departing Sharks since he was 16 and wants to "honour those boys" with his performance against the Roosters.

"I don't want to let them down and disappoint them, winning the game is the most important part of the week for me."

Katoa reveals Cowboys appeal

Sione Katoa has revealed North Queensland's attacking style was a major attraction behind his move to the Cowboys in 2027.

After helping eliminate his future club from the finals, Katoa told ESPN he "loves the style of footy" they play, describing it as "free footy" and similar to Cronulla's attack.

Katoa emotional over Sharks farewell
He also admitted the reality that every game could be his last for Cronulla is beginning to sink in.

"Tonight might have been the last week, maybe the last game," he told ESPN after scoring a double against North Queensland.

"I'm very happy right now that I get another week with my brothers and play again."

Cleary racing clock for preliminary final

Nathan Cleary is in doubt for Penrith's preliminary final after scans revealed an stress-related bone issue in his foot.

The Panthers will assess and monitor their star halfback over the next fortnight, with their week off providing valuable recovery time.

Cleary has, however, been cleared of any suspension concern after receiving only a Grade 1 Dangerous Contact charge for his incident with Hugo Savala.

stories.headline: Rams, Giants looking to build on disparate Week 1 showings when they meet on Monday night
stories.summary: — The Los Angeles Rams could not have looked worse, while the New York Giants
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- — The Los Angeles Rams could not have looked worse, while the New York Giants could not have looked better in their respective season openers.


Both sides recognize the response to those performances when they meet on Monday night will be just as important as their Week 1 showings.


“They understand, they understood going into the game that it was the first game of a 17-game season, no matter what the outcome is going to be, and that the Rams are going to be next up regardless of what the outcome is,” Giants coach John Harbaugh said. “So, our job is to get better, keep improving, because you have to.”


The Rams (0-1) have plenty to address following their 27-7 flop to the San Francisco 49ers in Melbourne, Australia. They were outplayed against their NFC West rivals after an offseason spent adding big names and amassing bigger expectations.


“That wasn’t a day that really any of us liked,” Rams coach Sean McVay said. “But, hey, it’s not final, and we’re looking to move forward.”


Among the priorities for McVay is getting his offense on track after quarterback Matthew Stafford looked nothing like the form that won him the Most Valuable Player award last season, completing 60% of his throws for 155 yards and one interception.


McVay cited a lack of consistency for those struggles, compounded because the Rams possessed the ball twice in the first quarter and once in the third quarter.


“How do we string together positive plays, both in the run and the pass together?,” McVay said. “And that’s what good offenses do, and that’s what we’re striving to do.”


The Giants (1-0) had no such problems, possessing the ball for 21:33 in the second half as they kept the high-powered Dallas Cowboys’ offense on the sideline in a 28-20 victory.


It is a game plan they want to repeat on a regular basis, ideally making New York punter Jordan Stout a viewer instead of an active participant.


“We want to be on the field as long as we can, eating up the clock, getting points after every drive,” fullback Patrick Ricard said.


“I told Jordan Stout, ‘You’re not punting this game.’ I was just trying to set the tone early for the season, and we punted once. So, this game and every game moving forward, we’re going to try (to have the) punter not punt.”


Need to know
New York Giants (1-0) at Los Angeles Rams (0-1)


When/where to watch: Monday, 8:15 p.m. EDT, ESPN/ABC


Latest odds: Rams by 7


Against the spread: Giants 1-0; Rams 0-1.


Last week: Giants beat the Cowboys 28-20; Rams lost to the 49ers 27-7.


Last meeting: Rams beat the Giants 26-25 on Dec. 31, 2023, in East Rutherford, New Jersey.


Series record: Rams lead 30-17.


Matchup to watch
Giants QB Jaxson Dart vs. Rams edge rushers Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart. Dart kept the Cowboys off balance, throwing for 230 yards and three touchdowns and rushing for 54 yards. And while he was sacked twice, they resulted in a 1-yard loss. Los Angeles doesn’t have Myles Garrett for the next four weeks following knee surgery, putting Stewart into the starting lineup opposite Young. The Rams couldn’t generate meaningful pressure on Niners QB Brock Purdy, so they have to be disruptive while also accounting for Dart’s ability to create outside of structure.


Stats and stuff
— McVay is 4-0 versus the Giants and can join George Allen, Chuck Knox, Dan Quinn and Dick Vermeil as coaches to win his first five games against them.


— Stafford failed to lead the Rams to at least 10 points for the second time as a starter, with both games coming against San Francisco (24-9 loss on Oct. 3, 2022).


— Dart’s three touchdown passes versus Dallas tied his career high (Oct. 19, 2025, against Denver).


— The Giants lost their only previous road game against the Rams at SoFi Stadium 17-9 on Oct. 4, 2020, with no fans in attendance because of the COVID-19 pandemic.


— This has been a series of streaks lately, with the Rams winning five in a row from 1994-2001, then the Giants taking the next seven from 2002-2016, and the Rams taking the past four going back to 2017.


— Harbaugh lost his first road game as coach of the Baltimore Ravens, 23-20 in overtime at the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sept. 29, 2008. That game was played on a Monday night.


— Giants RB Cam Skattebo had 81 yards rushing and a touchdown on 18 carries against the Cowboys, the second-best outing of his brief NFL career. He ran for 98 yards and three scores against Philadelphia on Oct. 9, 2025.


— The Giants went 1-7 on the road last season, defeating the Raiders in Las Vegas on Dec. 28, 2025, to kickstart their current three-game winning streak.

stories.headline: Nola dominates Mets in 3-0 win as Phillies tie Cubs for top NL wild card
stories.summary: — Aaron Nola allowed three hits over seven innings and the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Mets 3-0 Thursday night to tie the Chicago Cubs for the top NL wild card in a game interrupted by a scary collision that led to New York first baseman Jared...
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- — Aaron Nola allowed three hits over seven innings and the Philadelphia Phillies beat the Mets 3-0 Thursday night to tie the Chicago Cubs for the top NL wild card in a game interrupted by a scary collision that led to New York first baseman Jared Young being carted off the field.


Young was knocked down when pitcher Nolan McLean struck him on the head with a knee when the two converged for Justin Crawford’s slow grounder in the sixth. Young was motionless on the field after the collision and taken to a hospital. New York manager Andy Green said a CT scan was negative and Young had concussion symptoms.


Nola (7-10) didn't allow a hit until Nick Morabito singled with one out in the sixth. He struck out four and walked three, improving to 4-2 with a 2.07 ERA in his last 10 starts.


Jonathan Bowlan got two outs in the eighth before exiting due to right groin tightness with a 2-2 count on Francisco Lindor. Jhoan Duran pitched a one-hit ninth for his 32nd save in 34 chances, finishing the Phillies' major league-high 19th shutout.


Philadelphia is 85-68, the same as the Cubs. The Phillies closed within four games of NL East-leading Atlanta (89-64).


New York has been blanked 15 times.


Bryce Harper had an RBI single and Luis Arraez and Crawford had sacrifice flies as the Phillies.


McLean (11-10) allowed one run, seven hits and three walks in five innings while striking out fives.


Up next
Newly acquired RHP José Urquidy (2-2, 5.28 ERA) is expected to pitch for the Phillies in some capacity Friday against Mets LHP Zac Thornton (4-5, 3.44 ERA).

stories.headline: Jessica Shepard has 5th triple-double and the Wings beat the Sparks 97-77 for 5th straight win
stories.summary: — Paige Bueckers scored 19 points, Jessica Shepard had her fifth triple-double of the season with 13 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists, and the Dallas Wings beat the Los Angeles Sparks 97-77 on Thursday night for their fifth straight victory.
stories.body:
ARLINGTON, Texas -- — Paige Bueckers scored 19 points, Jessica Shepard had her fifth triple-double of the season with 13 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists, and the Dallas Wings beat the Los Angeles Sparks 97-77 on Thursday night for their fifth straight victory.


Both teams were returning from the break for the FIBA World Cup in Germany, where Bueckers helped lead the United States to the title.


Dallas (25-16) tied the franchise record for wins in a season set by the 2003 WNBA champion Detroit Shock (25-9). The Wings have three games remaining in the regular season.


Shepard has the third-most triple-doubles in a season in WNBA history, trailing Alyssa Thomas' six in the 2023 and eight in 2025.


Maddy Siegrist added 12 points and Arike Ogunbowale had 11 for Dallas. Kitija Laksa and Aziaha James each scored 10 off the bench. Odyssey Sims did not play in the fourth quarter after injuring her right knee late in the third.


Nneka Ogwumike scored 18 points to lead Los Angeles (12-26). Dearica Hamby added 14 points and Rae Burrell had 12.


Dallas pulled away by going on a 12-0 run spanning the third-quarter break for a 74-58 lead. The Wings finished with a 46-27 edge in rebounds.

stories.headline: Pelicans, Saddiq Bey agree on 3-year, $55.5M contract extension
stories.summary: The New Orleans Pelicans and forward Saddiq Bey have agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension, his agents tell ESPN.
stories.body:
New Orleans Pelicans forward Saddiq Bey has agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, a deal that also includes a trade kicker, his agents James Dunleavy and Jordan Gertler of Excel Sports Management tell ESPN.

Bey missed the 2024-25 season after sustaining a torn ACL while with the Atlanta Hawks but had a resurgent first full season back last year with New Orleans, averaging a career-high 17.7 points per game. He is now locked into a fully guaranteed deal through 2029-30 with the Pelicans.

Bey appeared in 72 games for the Pelicans last season, including 64 starts. On top of his career-best scoring average, Bey also averaged 5.6 rebounds and 2.5 assists per game.

Last season, Bey recorded three of the four highest-scoring games of his career during his bounce-back year with the Pelicans -- a 42-point effort against the Utah Jazz on Feb. 26, a 36-point outing against the Memphis Grizzlies on Jan. 23 and a 34-point night Jan. 31 against the Philadelphia 76ers.

He also averaged 20 points per game and shot 40% from the 3-point line after last season's All-Star break, according to ESPN Research, while also averaging career highs in both 2-point baskets attempted/made as well as free throws attempted/made each game.

Bey was originally drafted by the Detroit Pistons in the first round of the 2020 NBA draft.

In 364 career games with the Pistons, Hawks and Pelicans, Bey holds career averages of 14.8 points, 5.3 rebounds and two assists per game.

The Pelicans tip off their preseason schedule against the Oklahoma City Thunder on Oct. 6 and host the Indiana Pacers on Oct. 21 to open the regular season.

stories.headline: Marco Rose proud of 'Bournemouth football' in European debut win over Real Sociedad
stories.summary: Marco Rose was delighted to watch "Bournemouth football" during a 2-1 win at Real Sociedad and a memorable first match in Europe for the Premier League club.
stories.body:
Marco Rose was delighted to watch "Bournemouth football" during a 2-1 win at Real Sociedad and a memorable first match in Europe for the Premier League club.

First-half goals by Justin Kluivert and Rayan ensured the Cherries' first venture into a European competition ended with victory in the Europa League.

Tournament favourites Bournemouth had to withstand a second-half comeback from Real Sociedad, who reduced the deficit through Sergio Gómez and were indebted to a string of late saves by Đorđe Petrović to make sure the travelling 2,000 supporters went back to Boscombe happy.

"That's Bournemouth. That's Bournemouth football. We want to be active, we want to be front-footed, we want to play forward and we want to create chances. We had a header to be 3-0 up, but in the end a game is 90 minutes," Rose told TNT Sports.

"It was very intense and tough. In the end an enjoyable result. A brilliant first half in everything. Our effort, attitude and the way we won balls with our pressing, our out of possession game and our goals.

"A top first half. Second half we needed to suffer and we were not so sharp. In the end it was a deserved win but we need to talk about the second half."

Petrović made two fine stops to thwart Orri Óskarsson in the final five minutes at San Sebastian to secure a historic win for the Cherries, but Rose was eager to not brush under the carpet a difficult second half before his team sealed the second win of his reign.

Rose added: "It's about maybe the mindset and we lack a little bit of intensity. If you lose these kind of things, in our style, then you will get in trouble.

"That is what we have to know. If you get tired, we can change, we can do substitutes and we should do it a little bit better, but today it is just about a brilliant win away in our first European game.

"That's very important for the club and I have to say 2,000 fans from Bournemouth. I am quite happy for everyone at the club and our fans."

Adam Smith first joined Bournemouth in 2014 when they were in the third tier of English football and only 18 years ago the south coast outfit were on -17 points in League Two.

Smith told TNT Sports: "What a night. It's history made. I told the lads before the game, we're making history playing here tonight but we want to do it with a win and that's what we've done.

"The lads are absolutely buzzing and now it's a quick turnaround for Liverpool on Sunday.

"Yeah, I mean I think this is my 12th season and when I first joined, to think I'd be playing in Europe for this club, I would never have dreamed of that.

"It's an amazing achievement to get the win tonight and against a good team. Really looking forward to the next game on Sunday."

stories.headline: Messi, MLS' Garber appear to have heated exchange after Miami win
stories.summary: Lionel Messi pointed his finger at MLS commissioner Don Garber on multiple occasions while speaking with him after Inter Miami's game with Cruz Azul on Wednesday.
stories.body:
MIAMI -- Lionel Messi pointed his finger at MLS commissioner Don Garber on multiple occasions while speaking with him after Inter Miami's game with Cruz Azul on Wednesday.

stories.headline: GM: 'Door open' for star goalie Hellebuyck to remain with Jets
stories.summary: Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff didn't rule out the possibility that goaltender Connor Hellebuyck could remain with the team after going public with a trade demand. The Jets formally suspended Hellebuyck on Wednesday for failure to report to training camp.
stories.body:
Winnipeg Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff didn't rule out the possibility that star goaltender Connor Hellebuyck could remain with the team after going public with a trade demand.

The Jets formally suspended Hellebuyck on Wednesday for failure to report to training camp. The 33-year-old goaltender requested a trade during exit interviews after last season, his 11th with the franchise. Hellebuyck won the Hart Trophy as NHL MVP in 2025 and has won the Vezina Trophy as the NHL's top goaltender three times, being a finalist for the award five times.

"No doors are closed. He's a player that's under contract for five years. But at the end of the day, that's his choice," said Cheveldayoff at the opening of training camp on Thursday.

Cheveldayoff said there's no timeline for trading his star goaltender, something the Jets have been trying to do for "a long period of time," including during last June's NHL draft. While he pushed back on a report this week that categorized the offers for Hellebuyck as "terrible," the Jets GM said, "There's been nothing that's allowed us to say, 'OK, this works for both teams.'"

Hellebuyck and his agent made their trade demand public with a statement in late August, saying "I have tried to handle the situation quietly and respectfully while giving the organization time to explore its options" in trading him.

"When Connor requested being traded, we kept it quiet. That was partly on his request as well. And we tried to make that work and we've been trying to make that work ever since," Cheveldayoff said.

There's been a wave of speculation about why Hellebuyck has asked out of Winnipeg just two seasons into a seven-year contract extension that he signed in Oct. 2023.

Cheveldayoff was asked about comments Hellebuyck made about the "blowback" his wife Andrea received after the goaltender led Team USA to Olympic gold in the 2026 Winter Olympics over Team Canada. Hellebuyck attended the State of the Union Address with all but five of his teammates, where President Donald Trump announced that the goalie would be awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.

"What they endured, they shouldn't have had to," said Cheveldayoff of the social media abuse.

TSN reported this week that Hellebuyck will not waive his no-movement clause to join any of the six other Canadian NHL teams.

"I'm not going to get into the specific teams. My guess is to what his restrictions are in those regards. Again, the choices that he makes are the choices that he makes. I don't have an understanding as to why he made some of the choices that he made when talking about those kind of situations," Cheveldayoff said.

There's also been speculation about a "gentlemen's agreement" that might have been made between Cheveldayoff and Hellebuyck when the goalie re-signed in Winnipeg, that if he asked out during his contract, that request would be honored.

"A contract is a contract in the National Hockey League, period. There are no side agreements, there's no general agreements. The league doesn't allow for that. So I guess the fact is any notion around that would not have any merit," Cheveldayoff said.

The Jets GM was also asked if there was a "promise" made to Hellebuyck and Jets star center Mark Scheifele that the team would contend for the Stanley Cup annually when both players signed their extensions in Oct. 2023.

"Promise is an interesting word. We've been a team that's tried to be as competitive as we possibly can each and every year," he said.

But overall, the Jets GM wasn't looking to explore why Hellebuyck wanted out.

"I guess in my mind it's irrelevant. In my mind, I have to deal with the situation that's in front of me. Connor's made the choices and we'll just deal with him moving forward," he said.

The Jets GM addressed the challenge in trying to move Hellebuyck. Beyond finding a deal that helps Winnipeg stay competitive and Hellebuyck's trade protection, Cheveldayoff said it's a smaller market when trying to trade a No. 1 goalie vs. other positions.

"If you're a team that has a bona fide No. 1 goaltender and he's locked up and he's yours, you're probably not interested. And it's not disparaging Connor Hellebuyck or anything like that. It's just the goalie market in general," he said. "So the fact of the matter that a team might be on the list as an available option has a No. 1 goaltender, well, that's kind of a moot point."

Hellebuyck will begin losing salary if he's still suspended when the NHL regular season starts. His $8.5 million average annual value will not count against the Jets' salary cap.

stories.headline: Alexa Grasso shows off flyweight's elite status in women's P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
It's uncommon for two fighters ranked in the pound-for-pound top 10 to meet in a bout with no championship at stake. But that was the case at Saturday's fourth annual Noche UFC, where Alexa Grasso faced Manon Fiorot.

Grasso is a former women's flyweight champion and Fiorot competed for the belt last year, so their status as MMA elites was well established before they fought. And when Grasso won by unanimous decision, she further solidified her standing in the ESPN women's pound-for-pound rankings.

The top five of the rankings remains intact, and Grasso moves up from 10th to replace Fiorot at No. 6. Fiorot slips two positions to No. 8 in a pound-for-pound hierarchy in which seven of the 10 ranked women compete at flyweight (including Zhang Weili, the former UFC strawweight champion who last fought in an unsuccessful challenge of Valentina Shevchenko in November).

With Shevchenko injured and having vacated her title, there will be much scrambling for the top spot, which will be at stake when No. 5 Natalia Silva fights unranked Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 16. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

Carlos Contreras Legaspi: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Cyborg; 3. Zhang; 4. Dern; 5. Silva; 6. Grasso; 7. Ditcheva; 8. Suarez; 9. Fiorot; 10. Blanchfield.

Jeff Wagenheim: 1. Shevchenko; 2. Zhang; 3. Cyborg; 4. Silva; 5. Grasso; 6. Dern; 7. Fiorot; 8. Blanchfield; 9. Suarez; 10. Ditcheva.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

5. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

6. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Alexandre Pantoja

UFC flyweight

Record: 30-6

Last: L (TKO1) vs. Joshua Van, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Sept. 19 vs. Joshua Van

Pantoja became the UFC's unquestioned flyweight king by racking up four title defenses, including two in pay-per-view main events in 2024. He built his winning streak to eight in his UFC 317 win over Kai Kara-France, whom he had already defeated before, like other challengers. But he lost his belt in a gruesome way, injuring his elbow in the opening seconds of a UFC 323 fight with Van. Pantoja gets his rematch with Van at UFC 331.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight interim champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: TBA

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was heralded as the future of the generation when he broke onto the scene, but endured growing pains in losses to Ngannou and Jones. He looks formidable now, and no one will be counting him out if he faces Aspinall in a title unification bout.

10. Alex Pereira

UFC heavyweight / light heavyweight

Record: 13-4

Last: L (TKO2) vs. Ciryl Gane, June 14

Next: TBA

He was on the verge of making history when the opportunity fell apart. Pereira was a UFC champion at middleweight, then light heavyweight, but his unprecedented pursuit of a belt in a third weight class did not go well for the Brazilian, who lost an interim heavyweight title fight to Gane on the White House card. At 39 years old, Pereira does not have much time left to recapture the magic.

stories.headline: I raced against Max Verstappen ... for 10 seconds: Inside the chaos of Max vs 100
stories.summary: ESPN's Nate Saunders might not have lasted long in Max vs 100, but it was still a memorable event. Here, he reflects on his karting experience with Formula 1's Max Verstappen
stories.body:
Few can say they have raced against Max Verstappen -- even if they can only boast that they stayed in front of him for all of 10 seconds.

That was about as long as my challenge lasted in Max vs 100, a wonderfully simple concept on Disney+: put four-time world champion Verstappen at the back of a 101-kart grid at Silverstone and give him 30 laps to pass everybody in front of him. Once he passed you, your race was over.

Starting 89th, I was eliminated before my kart had even reached the front of the grid we were all racing from.

A humbling experience, no doubt: but should an amateur karter going up against one of the greatest drivers of all time have expected any different?

It wasn't just me who had a blink-and-you-missed-it moment against Verstappen. He dispatched an astonishing 64 drivers in that first lap alone and needed only 13 more to catch and overtake everyone else.

Verstappen enjoyed it so much he teased doing it again next year against 200. Seeing how quickly he got things done on Wednesday, you would not bet against him completing that challenge with a handful of laps to spare, either.

Starting as low as I did, there was probably not much chance of any other outcome for me. I already had the excuses ready to explain my lowly grid slot. A spin during one-shot qualifying had turned what was already a middling-to-below-average lap into one only good enough to occupy the 45th row of the grid. Shoot. A blow, I told myself, of getting down to Turn 1 in one piece and an even bigger blow for my chances of staying ahead of Verstappen for even a few corners. Perhaps a better lap and grid position would have given me a better buffer to prevent the inevitable, I reasoned, while Verstappen struggled to get past the slower karts in the field.

- Max vs 100: Verstappen jokes taking on '200' drivers next time

- Max Verstappen wins Max vs 100 in style after overtaking 100 go-karters

Turns out the excuses weren't necessary -- an improved grid spot wouldn't have made a shred of difference. As the red lights at the beginning of the start procedure went on one by one, Verstappen had rocked his kart backwards and forwards in a bouncing motion, an old trick he said he learned racing as a seven-year-old. It meant his kart was already rolling well enough to breeze past the karts nearest to him as the lights turned green.

I knew no such tricks, so like the majority of the other amateurs, moved off the line sluggishly as I set about looked for a racing line through the blur of cars down towards Turn 1.

Approximately 10 seconds later, as some space opened up around me as I came off the curve and onto the straight, I glanced to my right.

There he was.

And then, he wasn't.

Verstappen breezed on by as though he was driving a different category of vehicle altogether. As that part of the field got to the first corner, karts were spinning left and right, but he threaded through the chaos like a slalom skier, at one stage simply taking to the grass when the conventional route vanished. My own kart got turned around -- perhaps because I was as much watching the disappearing Verstappen as I was the disappearing bit of unoccupied tarmac in front of me. It is easy to forget when watching trackside or TV the remarkable control of a vehicle professionals had -- Verstappen seemed to be racing on rails, even when he was driving off track to pass karts facing the wrong way.

So that was it. 10 seconds after racing Verstappen had started, my race against Verstappen was over. Brutal stuff indeed.

It all happened so fast that some of the 64 who slowly trundled back into the pit lane after elimination were not even convinced they had seen Verstappen go by. By the time I was out of the kart, he was up to 20th.

"I think the first lap went a bit better than expected, so that helps a lot," Verstappen said later.

Organisers had set a limit of 30 laps but that seemed ludicrously generous as he scythed his way through the field. There had been talk beforehand about trying to defend, working together or even making Verstappen fight for each position. When asked about advice for the 100 karters ahead of the event, Verstappen's long-time rival George Russell had joked that participants should try and go four or five-wide and effectively block the road to stop him advancing. There was, of course, not even the slightest bit of coordination between anyone at the back of the field once the lights went out. Even if we had, Verstappen appeared more than happy to take to the grass on a couple of occasions to get to where he needed to be.

"You just act on instinct, whatever happens when the lights go out, you kind of just see where the gaps are and then you also kind of need to trust the few people around you that they don't do anything crazy," Verstappen said later. "But to be honest, they didn't."

Even if no-one was driving like crazy, the chaos at the start was predictable. Race director and circuit designer David Terrien -- who raced against Max's parents Jos Verstappen and Sophie Kumpen when they were junior karters -- later said he doubted there has ever been a kart race featuring 101 karts. That's not surprising, as there did not seem to be quite enough road to accommodate everyone at the beginning. The grid stretched down the main straight and around a curve. The first lap was almost immediately put under caution -- there were spins, mine included, at Turn 1, while two karts crashed at Turn 3 further up the track so badly that a group of 10 karts got stuck behind.

The circuit worked well when the field had been trimmed down, though, with Verstappen's progress slowing as the amateurs on track were wittled down. He spent six laps in fourth, slowly reeling in the runaway trio at the front.

Verstappen ended up beating one journalist who did, at least, manage to do a better job of representing for the F1 paddock: Dutch reporter Jacky Martens, who finished ahead of YouTuber Zac Alsop and Red Bull's own Lewis Osler to be crowned best of the amateurs. Those last laps were entertaining to watch on the stream, as Verstappen got to utilise the microphones he had fitted to his balaclava to talk to the other competitors around him. "I'm coming for you," he said to a contestant at one stage. Later, he told commentators Alex Jacques and Matt Gallagher: "They need to focus because I'm definitely catching them."

Several of those who remained at least got to properly experience what racing Verstappen is all about. Late in the contest, one of the racers joked to Verstappen -- via a microphone which linked the Dutchman to drivers he approached -- that all he could hear in his head was the famous song about him: "Duh Duh Duh Duh, Max Verstappen, Duh Duh Duh Duh."

Another turned to Verstappen as he approached, laughing and putting his hands together as if begging him not to overtake. He's not the only one to have felt like this with the Dutchman approaching him at alarming speed. McLaren CEO Zak Brown joked last year, as Verstappen started reeling in McLaren pair Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri in the championship, that Verstappen was like the T-Rex in Jurassic Park, seen chasing the car in the mirror with the warning 'Objects in the mirror are closer than they appear.' My experience of being passed by Verstappen was so quick I didn't even get the chance to experience the fear.

For Verstappen, it seemed like enormous fun -- he later said he had not driven a proper go-kart since 2016. In a year which has seen Verstappen's love of Formula 1 tested on a massive scale, he later joked he would cherish his winners' trophy as it was his first of the year so far.

Verstappen recently signed a contract to stay in Formula 1 with Red Bull into 2030, ending several years of speculation about moves elsewhere. It's perhaps not surprising he can't imagine a future away from the company which first brought him into Formula 1 as a 17-year-old in 2015. "It's just great that with Red Bull they always come up with some crazy fun things and it suits me as well," he said. "I can really be myself and I think also the way it was organised today, I know that it requires a lot of effort to be able to do something like this."

Whether I'll be there on the grid with him for a future event remains to be seen -- if Wednesday's contest had been an audition to race against a Formula 1 legend again, I dismally failed.

But, given how Verstappen did make almost 100 people look like complete amateurs, there doesn't seem to be too much shame in that.

stories.headline: Borussia Dortmund teenager Konstantinos Karetsas returns to training after Champions League health scare
stories.summary: Borussia Dortmund says 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.
stories.body:
Borussia Dortmund have said 18-year-old midfielder Konstantinos Karetsas is back in training just over a week after he slumped to the ground in an alarming medical incident on his Champions League debut.

Karetsas passed the ball to a teammate then signaled his distress to the referee before sitting on the grass during Dortmund's 3-2 win over Villarreal on Sept. 8.

He was in tears as he was stretchered off with suspected circulatory problems and was then taken to a hospital, where he stayed for much of last week.

"Konstantinos Karetsas is back in team training as of Wednesday after doing individual sessions at the start of the week," Dortmund said. "It was his first joint session with his teammates after he was taken off with circulatory problems in the game against Villarreal."

Dortmund hasn't specified the nature of any diagnosis for Karetsas, who was signed from Genk for a reported fee of $34.6 million last month, and didn't indicate whether he would be able to play Saturday against Stuttgart in the Bundesliga.

Karetsas plays internationally for Greece but was born in Belgium, where local media have reported that dehydration was suspected as a factor.

"I'm doing really well," he said in a video recorded during a visit to his old club Genk and published Monday on X. "We tested everything and everything is fine. I just need to adjust a bit to the intensity but that will come with time."

"I went out with him but in that moment, he wasn't able to speak," Book said.

- Borussia Dortmund teenager Karetsas hospitalised after slumping to turf in Champions League

Karetsas was able to cheer on his teammates from the stands in Saturday's 3-0 win over Paderborn.

Managing director Lars Ricken said there had been "no warning signs" of any circulatory problems prior to the incident.

stories.headline: 'Deeper connection': Clark finds true self at Warriors
stories.summary: Warriors lock Erin Clark found form and his identity after his move from the battling Gold Coast to become one of the best players in his position in the NRL.
stories.body:
Erin Clark has emerged as one of the game's best locks and Warriors legend Clinton Toopi says it's due to a re-discovery of who he is as a footballer.

The 29-year-old will start in the No.13 jersey against Newcastle in an elimination final at Eden Park on Sunday a transformed footballer, after being chopped and changed by the underperforming Gold Coast outfit for five seasons.

"When he was at the Titans I think Erin lost his identity in terms of who he is," Toopi told AAP.

"Am I a hooker? Am I a lock? Am I a bench player? Psychologically in those moments you are happy to play anywhere, but when given responsibility to own a starting position it's a huge confidence booster.

"Coach Andrew Webster has got the best out of all the players and Erin has shown that he wants to own that lock position."

In the past two seasons at the Warriors, across 50 games, Auckland-born Clark has averaged 135m compared to the 65m he managed at the Titans.

Incredibly he has notched 2686 post-contact metres in two Warriors seasons, well above the 2113m he made in 94 Titans games.

The New Zealand international started his career in the Warriors system and played NSW Cup in the halves. After playing one NRL game for the club he moved to the Titans where he played well but was never offered a regular starting spot.

After one match off the bench for the Warriors last season, he has played the last 49 in the No.13 jersey without missing a game.

"Erin would admit to that deeper connection coming back home for a second time," Toopi said.

"He has spread his wings and come back and flourished to become one of the game's elite and best in terms of what he offers."

While the Warriors players are part of a tightly run system, Clark naturally has attacking gifts that add to the powerful running and aggressive defence in the middle that has made him such a fearsome proposition.

"In his past he was a little nuggety six but didn't get a chance to play at any stage there with the Titans," Toopi said.

"When you play six for a long time it tells you that you have vision, skill and you are a runner.

"What Erin has been able to do at the Warriors is exploit those talents and show what skillset he can bring to the table. You see him go to the line and get short balls away.

"He has got an offload, he powers through, he has got a flick pass. He has got a grubber. He has been given the OK to do that."

Toopi, who suffered the heartbreak of losing the 2002 decider to the Sydney Roosters, explained what was required in a do-or-die final.

"I got caught up in the atmosphere of the 2002 grand final. You walk out on the field and there are 90,000 going crazy and all I could do was be in awe of the moment," Toopi said.

"Before you know it that 80 minutes is over and you have lost a grand final. It still is very raw 20-odd years later. These Warriors boys will want to walk off the field having no regrets at all."
